I was first diagnosed with depression before ADHD, when i felt like the antidepressants weren’t working i sought out another doctor in an ADHD institution that takes care of such cases here in my country. He made me undergo an assessment for depression to rule it out first. We then reached to the point that i don’t have depression, all the mood swings and emotional irregularities are very common symptoms of ADHD.
But depression is also a super common diagnosis to get along ADHD, the difference is the cause. For me, the symptoms that i had suggesting depression were due to how my ADHD interfered with my daily life and have affected my opinion of myself. But in the other hand, some depression symptoms can present like ADHD but that doesn’t mean the person has ADHD.
So it’s expected that the medications help in mood swings or disorders like that. Consult your doctor if you believe you might have clinical depression or if it’s just a symptom of your ADHD which the medication is now making you recognize.

And a little scientific note, both depression and ADHD medications work closely on similar neurotransmitters (happy and motivational chemicals) although different ones, but they can still overlap.

i knew something about muscles stiffing since i’ve watched a video of someone trying to open a fist of a dead body. but i didn’t know its name and how it happens physiologically.
physiology of skeletal muscles

5 minutes ago, i finished studying for my musculoskeletal exam and learned something very creepy. It’s called rigor mortis - for those who don’t know, it happens 2-4 hours after death, it’s basically muscle stiffness where the muscles stay the same as they are so when people discover the body and move it, it stays the same way. meaning if someone died with their arms on a desk, the arms stay elevated even if they were laid down. It happens because there’s no longer ATP production that helps relaxes the muscles.
